# Érica Menin

> Staff Design Systems Designer with 15+ years in design. Érica works on design systems for people and AI: component audits, Figma and code alignment, tokens, documentation, and the guidance agents need to use a system well. Brazilian, based in Germany, remote-first.

Érica gets excited about taking messy, complex things and making them work. For a long time that has meant design systems. Now that AI reads them too, she is working through what a system needs so that people and agents can both use it correctly, and writing about the wins, the awkward moments, and the "well, that didn't work" parts at Design Systems Unfiltered.

She is open to staff-level design systems roles and freelance projects.

Contact: erica@menin.me · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ericamenin/)

## What she is exploring

Her current position on design systems and AI. Subject to change… things move SO fast.

- What does AI need beyond tokens and components? Tokens give values and component properties give options, but neither explains when to use something or why an exception exists. That lives in documentation and component contracts: expected behavior, allowed combinations, accessibility requirements.
- How much guidance is enough? Less than you'd think. A short AGENTS.md that points to where everything else lives, rules that grow each time the agent gets something wrong, and lint rules for what really matters.
- Where do busy teams start? A quick health check, then one problem that keeps coming back. One fix. One check. Then the next.
- What comes after "AI-ready"? Once a system is in good shape, agents can maintain parts of it: spot what no longer matches after a component changes, fix it, and open a pull request. People define what's "right" and test for it. That is the idea behind an agentic design system.

## Work

- [Getting a design system back in sync](https://ericamenin.com/design-system-back-in-sync): An audit of 62 components across Figma, React, and Flutter, followed by changes to the Figma libraries, variables, themes, and migration guidance.
- [Maturing a design system beyond components](https://designsystemsunfiltered.substack.com/p/my-last-year-as-a-design-system-designer): A look back at a year of library changes, pattern documentation, support tracking, and day-to-day work with product designers.
- [AI + Design Systems](https://ericamenin.com/ai-design-systems): A design system built only for people is easy for AI to get wrong.
- [The Design System Advent Calendar](https://ericamenin.com/design-system-calendar): A small design system insight for every day until Christmas, hosted on Figma Sites.
- [soniq Design System](https://ericamenin.com/soniq-design-system) (earlier work, 2020–2023): A shared Figma library for web and mobile, with component documentation, pattern workshops, and regular reviews with developers.

## Writing

[Design Systems Unfiltered](https://designsystemsunfiltered.substack.com/) is Érica's Substack about design systems and AI.

- [Don't make your design system AI-ready yet](https://designsystemsunfiltered.substack.com/p/dont-make-your-design-system-ai-ready): A starting point for improving how AI works with an existing system, without beginning with a complete rebuild.
- [AI is shipping UI faster than your design system can protect it](https://designsystemsunfiltered.substack.com/p/ai-is-shipping-ui-faster-than-your): Repeated primary buttons, competing colors, and the wrong default background, and the decisions missing from the documentation.
- [I turned my biggest design system headache into my first Cursor command](https://designsystemsunfiltered.substack.com/p/how-a-project-that-haunted-me-led): Creating a first command and skill, and figuring out where AI could help with day-to-day design systems work.
